newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zaire accepts U.N. peace plan - Belgium.
newsitem.headline: Zaire accepts U.N. peace plan - Belgium.

text.p: Zaire has approved a United Nations plan designed to end the crisis in the African nation, the Belgian foreign ministry said on Wednesday.
"We are pleased to see that Mr Kamanda has confirmed that his country has approved a five-point United Nations plan...," ministry spokesman Andre Querton told a weekly news briefing.
He said Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke had met his Zairean counterpart Kamanda Wa Kamanda on Monday.

Zaire has accused the regular armies of Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi of fomenting an almost five-month-old Tutsi-led rebellion in eastern Zaire and of actively participating in fighting on Zairean soil.
All three countries deny the allegations.
Querton said Belgium was aware of human rights violations by both parties in the conflict.
"We have (now) received other witness accounts on major violations of human rights in the region," he said.
He reiterated Belgium was calling for U.N observers to be sent to the troubled region.
"We believe that (rebel chief Laurent) Kabila has accepted the principle," he added.
